title: Combination therapy with a novel CD2-targeted costimulatory bispecific antibody overcomes limitations of CD3 T cell engager treatment for solid tumors
one_line: Evotech built a non-blocking, Fc-silenced HER2xCD2 costimulatory bispecific that, dosed alongside a sub-efficacious EpCAMxCD3 TCE (solitomab), restores tumour killing with far less cytokine release than a CD28-based equivalent.
key_claims: The CD2 arm is a positive allosteric modulator: rather than blocking CD58 (as clinical-stage siplizumab does), it increases CD2-CD58 binding more than two-fold while supplying artificial costimulation.
Adding HER2xCD2 to a 2-5 pM sub-efficacious dose of the EpCAMxCD3 TCE restored T cell activation and improved killing ~10-fold in vitro.
In humanized B2M NOG mice with established BT-474 clone 5 HER2+ tumours, 10 ug/kg TCE alone gave complete remission in 1 of 9 mice versus 8 of 9 with HER2xCD2 co-treatment.
Against CRISPR-Cas9 CD58-knockout tumour cells (a documented escape route), the combination boosted TCE killing efficacy 25-35-fold by physically bridging T cell and tumour.

At matched killing, HER2xCD2 raised IL-6, TNF and IL-2 only up to 2-fold (interferon gamma up to 9-fold) versus up to 200-fold (interferon gamma 84-fold) for a HER2xCD28 bispecific, and CD2 also engaged CD28-negative CD8 T cells that the CD28 bispecific could not.
limitations: Efficacy demonstrated only in a humanized xenograft model lacking human stroma, chemokine gradients and pre-existing immune memory, so clinical translation is unproven.
This is a proof-of-concept HER2xCD2 molecule paired with solitomab, a TCE that was itself discontinued clinically; no clinical or patient data are presented.
Toxicity read-out is in vitro cytokine release, not in vivo CRS or on-target/off-tumour safety in a system with normal HER2-expressing tissue.
Whether amplifying endogenous CD2-CD58 binding rather than blocking it risks loss of pharmacological control was not directly tested.
No dose-ranging or durability/resistance follow-up beyond the reported complete remissions.
open_questions: Does independent dosing of the CD2 costimulator preserve efficacy at TCE doses low enough to avoid dose-limiting toxicity in patients?
Would the cytokine advantage over CD28 costimulation hold in an in vivo CRS-competent model or first-in-human study?
Can the modular two-drug concept be generalised to other tumour antigens and TCE pairs, including mismatched antigen combinations?
How much of the benefit comes from CD2 costimulation versus simple physical bridging, as suggested by the CD58-knockout result?
